What we do
What we do
Professional vibration mounts for every marine engine.

We manufacture professional vibration mounts for the marine engines of Yanmar, Volvo Penta, Cummins, Caterpillar, MAN, Perkins, Beta Marine, Mercruiser, John Deere and many other brands, together with bronze and fiber shaft bearings.

Working with us is simple. Tell us your engine model, or send a photo of your old mount if you are not sure. We check the part number, stud thread and mounting dimensions, and confirm the right mount before you order.

Your order is packed for international transport and leaves within 24 hours with FedEx or UPS Express, insured and tracked. It usually reaches you in 2–4 business days, depending on destination and customs.

Technical introduction
Technical introduction
From vibration to silence.

A diesel engine shakes with every firing stroke. An engine mount is a rubber spring between the engine and the hull: it carries the weight of the engine and gearbox, keeps the shaft in line and stops most of the vibration before it reaches the boat.

Inside a Novibrasyon mount

  1. 1
    StudCarries the engine foot.
  2. 2
    Adjusting nutsSet the engine height for shaft alignment.
  3. 3
    Rubber elementAbsorbs the vibration. Its hardness is given in Shore.
  4. 4
    Metal housingHolds the rubber and takes the load.
  5. 5
    Base flangeBolted to the engine bed.
  6. 6
    Centre coreThe raised centre of the base plate, bonded into the rubber.

Choosing the right mount

1Engine modelFind your engine in the engine finder (page 6). It shows the right mount for your engine.
2Load at each mountEngine and gearbox weight, shared between the mounts. The rear mounts often carry more, because the gearbox sits there.
3FitStud thread, mounting hole centers and height must match your engine feet and engine bed.
4Rubber hardnessChosen by the load at each mount: softer for light loads, harder for heavy ones.

Rubber hardness in Shore

softerharder
45ShoreSoftBest isolation, for lighter loads.
55ShoreMediumBalanced isolation and load capacity.
65ShoreHardFirm support for the heaviest loads.

When is it time to replace?

  • Cracked, split or crumbling rubber
  • Rubber coming away from the metal
  • The engine sits lower than before or the mount has collapsed
  • Soft, swollen rubber from oil or diesel
  • More vibration or noise, knocking when shifting gear
  • Shaft seal or shaft bearing wearing fast, shaft out of line

Mounts age together: when one has failed, check all of them. After fitting new mounts, check the shaft alignment at the coupling and tighten the nuts to the recommended torque.
